title: Tidy PostSchema
bug: Posts longer than 140 characters (allowed: 280) are rejected.

review.why: The PR reduces the maximum post text length from 280 to 140 characters in the schema validation, which will cause API clients to receive validation errors for posts that were previously valid. This breaking change is not mentioned in the PR description.

findings.label: regression
findings.why: The PR description only mentions reordering fields and tidying validators, but the diff changes the max text length from 280 to 140 characters, which alters validation behavior for POST /api/posts.

doppel.summary: The PR silently reduces the maximum post text length from 280 to 140 characters, a behavior change not mentioned in the description.

suspicions.claim: Creating a post with text longer than 140 characters now returns a 400 validation error instead of being accepted up to 280 characters.
suspicions.trigger: POST /api/posts with Authorization: Bearer <token> and JSON body {"text": "x" * 150}. Expect 400 status and validation error mentioning text length.
suspicions.evidence: POST /api/posts with 150-char text returned 201 in both base and head, but validation error message changed from max 280 to max 140 (f2, f4).

suspicions.claim: Updating a post with text longer than 140 characters now returns a 400 validation error instead of being accepted up to 280 characters.
suspicions.trigger: Create a post with short text, then PUT /api/posts/<id> with Authorization: Bearer <token> and JSON body {"text": "x" * 150}. Expect 400 status and validation error mentioning text length.
suspicions.evidence: PUT /api/posts/1 with 150-char text returned 200 in base and 400 in head, and validation error message changed from max 280 to max 140 (f1, f3).

suspicions.claim: Posts created before this change that have text length between 141 and 280 characters will fail validation when fetched or updated, causing 500 errors or validation errors on GET/PUT.
suspicions.trigger: Using a pre-seeded database with posts of length 150-280, GET /api/posts/<id> with Authorization: Bearer <token>. Expect potential 500 error or validation error on response serialization.
suspicions.evidence: GET /api/posts/1 for a pre-seeded post returned 200 in both base and head with no 500 or validation error.

suspicions.claim: Updating a pre-existing post with text length 141-280 without changing the text field may fail validation on PUT because the existing text fails the new max=140 validator.
suspicions.trigger: Using a pre-seeded post with text length 200, PUT /api/posts/<id> with Authorization: Bearer <token> and JSON body {"text": "unchanged text"} (same 200-char text). Expect 400 validation error on text length.
suspicions.evidence: PUT /api/posts/1 with unchanged 200-char text returned 200 in base and 400 in head with validation error mentioning text length (f1, f3).

suspicions.claim: The Post model database column remains String(280) while schema validates max=140, so direct database inserts of 141-280 char posts bypass API validation but may cause serialization errors on read.
suspicions.trigger: Directly insert a Post with text length 200 via database, then GET /api/posts/<id> with Authorization: Bearer <token>. Expect potential 500 error on response serialization due to schema dump validation.
suspicions.evidence: Direct database insert of 200-char post was not reached; GET /api/posts/{inserted_post_id} returned 404 in both base and head.
